paper_title: First Searches for Axions and Axion-Like Particles with the LUX Experiment
notes: Headline result: 90% C.L. upper limit on the axion-electron coupling g_Ae from solar axions with LUX 2013 data (95 live days x 118 kg), g_Ae < 3.5e-12, quoted in the abstract, Sec. V and Summary. The limit is flat in mass because the solar axion flux (Redondo 2013) is computed for a massless axion, stated to be valid for m_A < 1 keV/c^2; Fig. 6 plots the flat red limit line over m_A = 1e-5 to 1 keV/c^2 (0.01 eV to 1000 eV), which is the range reported here. The value 3.5e-12 is taken from the text; the flat line in Fig. 6 is consistent with it. The limit does not depend on the local dark matter density (solar flux source), hence dm_density_assumed is null. The paper also reports a secondary limit on galactic ALP dark matter over 1-16 keV/c^2 (g_Ae <= 4.2e-13 across the range, Fig. 7), not reported here as it is not the headline curve.
